items.author: yourQuantGuy

evidence.quote: 每个交易所之间或多或少都会有系统性的资金费率差别，比如过去一个月，BTC在Gate的资金费率年化是5.76%，而在Hyperliquid是8.64%。
这3%不到的潜在收益如果想要通过在交易所两边开仓套利是不容易捕捉的，因为有资金利用率、合约仓位开仓磨损等原因，即使加上杠杆，也无法线形提高收益。
无需开合约的仓位，通过boros的资金费率市场交易直接获得类似的资金费率敞口。
- spread 像YT，并不是固定收益的，且有可能亏损，但是对于本金来说，收益率可以非常高。如果想要参与，一定要研究清楚了。
- 四腿套利策略像PT，只要持有到期就有固定收益。
非常有意思的是，spread和四腿策略在订单薄上也是有点像YT和PT的关系，两者刚好相对，互相提供流动性。所以最近大家也可以看到支持spread的几个boros市场的流动性会有好一些。

items.summary: jukan05举onsemi、Microchip先例：其LTSA虽称有法律约束，需求下滑后仍允许客户改期、延后1–2年提货，据此质疑存储厂LTA能否护住下行期盈利。aleabitoreddit引MU称战略客户协议不可单方取消。
items.author: jukan05
items.new_information: onsemi、Microchip改期先例对比MU不可取消表态

evidence.quote: On October 30, 2023, on the Q3 earnings call, onsemi cut its SiC shipment forecast for the year from $1 billion to more than $800 million after one automotive OEM reduced demand. An analyst asked how this could happen when the company had been saying its LTSAs were legally binding. The same CEO reaffirmed that they were binding, but said he did not want to

enforce the contracts just to push inventory onto a customer whose demand had dropped. If it worked for both sides, terms could be adjusted customer by customer, whether by a quarter, a year, or longer.

Microchip is another case. Customers in its Preferred Supply Program (PSP) originally had to place 12 months of orders and could not cancel or reschedule them unless Microchip raised prices. On its November 2025 earnings call, however, the CEO said the company had accepted some cancellations and pushouts so customers could adjust their backlog. On the same

call, the CFO separately addressed the multiyear LTSAs the company had signed. Some of those contracts were still in effect, he said, but customers had been allowed to defer taking delivery of committed volumes by one to two years if they needed to.

The LTA itself may never be broken and may stay in place. But if both sides agree to push this year's volumes into next year or two years out, this year's earnings estimates come down. If price gets renegotiated too, margin estimates have to come down as well.
$MU: “strategic customer agreements cannot be unilaterally canceled.
Customers are obligated to pay for their committed volumes whether they take delivery or not.”

items.new_information: 所谓3D DRAM指替代SRAM的逻辑芯片内缓存，而非商品DRAM

evidence.quote: This doesn't make sense. As far as I know, TSMC has been working on this project for more than five years, but it would be a mistake to assume what they're building is commodity DRAM. TSMC has no DRAM IP, no DRAM patents, and none of the relevant technology.

At the 2025 VLSI Symposium, TSMC presented a memory technology based on oxide semiconductors, using a cell made of one transistor and one capacitor (1T1C). The goal was to integrate this memory into advanced logic chips and give processors a cache with low power and low latency.
The key feature of the design is that the memory array is built directly into the back end of line (BEOL) interconnect layers of the logic chip. Conventional DRAM is manufactured as a separate chip.
So TSMC would be producing 3D DRAM as a next generation technology to replace SRAM. And not in large volumes, either.
Anyone saying TSMC will make DDR or LPDDR has no idea what they're talking about.

And yes, it’s the same reporter who wrote the Intel JV story that TSMC publicly pushed back on. This is another bullshit leap. Exploring 3D DRAM is one thing. Mass-producing DDR or LPDDR and competing with the Big Three is a completely different business.
My read is that this is short bait for memory stocks. I’m surprised how many people are already treating it like a confirmed production plan.

Aero enables emissions to be directed as a forward looking bet rather than displayed as a backwards looking snapshot. This means Aero will attract more liquidity when organic market forces deem it's actually needed, which means tigher spreads, which means more volume routed through Aero, which means more fees for sAERO stakers.

evidence.quote: On Thursday, PSI published a proof generated by an AI research system running an unreleased Anthropic model. A human lead audited it, and the Lean proof assistant verified it line by line. The Stanford group that proved a special case in August has reviewed it and called it a huge result.

Here is what it proves, for yes-or-no questions about random, structureless inputs, a quantum computer can read exponentially fewer bits than a classical one only if the input has a rare pattern. On random data, the advantage is at most polynomial.

Though it doesn't touch structured problems, Shor’s algorithm breaks RSA by exploiting the hidden periodicity in numbers. Simulating molecules for drugs and batteries exploits the physics of the molecule itself. Those were always the targets, and the theorem says nothing about them.

It also only covers decision problems, in 2022, Yamakawa and Zhandry proved that for search problems, quantum computers can hold an exponential advantage eve relative to a random oracle. The two results are consistent, and their paper says so.

Today Physical Superintelligence PBC is announcing a proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, one of the central open problems in quantum complexity, with major implications for quantum computing speedup.
